title.en: Our home: Earth, a unique life-sustaining planet

text.en: There may be billions of planets in the universe, but life as we know it exists only on Earth. What makes Earth special?

Earth is at the right distance from the Sun, so its temperature allows liquid water, and this region is called the habitable zone.
Earth has four connected spheres: the lithosphere (rocks and land), hydrosphere (water), atmosphere (air) and biosphere (life).
Most of Earth's surface is covered by water, but only a small part of it is fresh water we can drink.
The atmosphere has layers, and the one nearest the ground, the troposphere, holds the air we breathe and the weather.
The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs harmful ultraviolet rays from the Sun.
The atmosphere acts like a blanket: gases such as carbon dioxide trap heat, which is the greenhouse effect, and it keeps Earth warm enough for life.
Burning fossil fuels adds extra carbon dioxide, which makes Earth warmer; this is global warming and it changes climate.
Changes in climate cause melting ice, rising seas, floods, droughts and stronger storms.
Carbon, water and nutrients cycle between the spheres, which keeps life going.
We can protect our home by saving energy, planting trees, reducing waste and using clean energy.

problem.en: Name the sphere: (a) a river, (b) a mountain, (c) a bird, (d) the wind.

text.en: A river is part of the hydrosphere.
A mountain is part of the lithosphere, and a bird is in the biosphere.

prompt.en: Why is the greenhouse effect both useful and harmful?

requiredIdeas.en: Natural greenhouse gases keep Earth warm.
Extra gases from fossil fuels trap too much heat.

points.en: Earth has the right distance, water and air for life.
Extra greenhouse gases cause global warming, which we can reduce.
